rows.author: G039
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino in celebration of the 148th
death anniversary of Gat Andres Bonifacio, the founder of Katipunan who led the revolution against the country´s Spanish colonizers, Rep. Ejercito stressed the need for Filipinos to preserve the spirit of nationalism, develop and preserve their historical sites, and allow the national government to be the repository of
the personal artifacts of Philippine national heroes. He thereafter informed his colleagues that during his term as mayor of San Juan City, he ensured the maintenance of the Pinaglabanan Shrine, as well as the construction of the monuments of Gat Bonifacio and Emilio Jacinto, the Museo ng Katipunan and the San Juan City Hall. Even as he lamented that said construction
evoked criticism and negative reaction from the informal settlers who were relocated as a
result thereof, he emphasized the desire of the people of San Juan to celebrate the 150th birth anniversary of Gat Bonifacio during the last week of November, 2013; to underscore the importance of the 1896 Philippine revolution that began in Pinaglabanan, San Juan; and to declare the place as Bonifacio and Jacinto
Shrine so that said celebration can be held
therein.
(House Journal No. 27, p.5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-11-28)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G084
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sarmiento spoke about the success of the
tree planting activities that he spearheaded in his province first on January 11, 2011 and which he followed through on November 11, 2011. After emphasizing the importance and beauty of trees, he urged his colleagues to actively participate in the government program aimed at planting 1.5 billion trees in about 1.5 million hectares of land by 2016 so that they would be able to fulfill the imperative task in mitigating climate change. He likewise thanked and
commended those who participated and made the
event a success, including the Department of Environment and Natural Resources for providing the saplings that they planted.
(House Journal No. 27,p.5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-11-28)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate commitee.

rows.author: G063
rows.title_short: His Gratitude To All His Supporters
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Benaldo, the Chair recognized
Rep. Emmanuel D. Pacquiao from the Lone District of Sarangani who initially expressed his
gratitude to everyone for their support, cheers and prayers during his recent boxing match against Juan Manuel Marquez. He also thanked his colleagues in the House and Speaker Belmonte for their commendation as embodied in Resolution No. 187 which they recently adopted. He pointed out that in his boxing bout with Marquez, he had shown more determination to prevail against all odds and had displayed that nothing scares him to achieve his dream and that no obstacles
and hardships would stop him from achieving his
goal for his beloved country and people. 
Speaking in Filipino, he advised the people who were not satisfied with his victory that the boxing ring sometimes resembles real life, where there comes a time when the road to success would be hard but that what matters most is the determination of people to face and overcome challenges.
(House Journal No. 27, p.5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-11-28)
rows.remarks: Manifestation of Rep. Cagas. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G009
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Kaka J. Bag-ao
from Party-List Akbayan rose to inform the Body of the alarming increase in new human immuno deficiency virus (HIV) infections in the country while most countries all over the world were starting to curb their HIV epidemics. She attributed the current spike to the complacency, ignorance and sectarian triumphalism that prevailed during the Arroyo administration
but also cited several other contributing
factors and deplored the lack of sufficient government funds for HIV treatment and AIDS program. She claimed that the reluctance of Health Secretary Enrique Ona to make additional requisition for funds was due itself to the government´s reliance on the allocations from an international funding agency named Global Fund which provides the Philippines with funding support for the treatment of diseases such as HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria. With the cancellation by Global Fund of its next round of grants to the Philippines by 2012, Rep. Bagao
pointed out that the Philippine government would
suffer adverse consequences in its HIV/AIDS prevention, treatment and support services to the extent that several Members decided to file House Bill No. 5312 to amend Republic Act (R..A.) No. 8504 which governs the country´s HIV and AIDS response, in order to ensure that said response would be properly funded. She then urged Congress to exercise political leadership and immediately act on the problem.
(House Journal No.27,p.6)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-11-28)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F016
rows.title_full: BENEFITS OF VOLUNTEERISM IN ALL SECTORS OF SOCIETY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cajayon rose on the occasion of the International Volunteer Day and the 10th anniversary of the International Year of Volunteers. She stressed that volunteerism has been an enormous renewable source for social, economic and environmental problem-solving throughout the world, and cited as examples
the volunteer work seen in the wake of the
Japanese earthquake and tsunami and in the Philippines´ Gawad Kalinga mass housing projects.
She informed the Body that in support for the
10th anniversary of the International Year of Volunteers, she filed House Resolution No. 686 with the intention that more people would be encouraged to support the cause of volunteerism in their respective communities. She thereafter thanked the Committee on People´s Participation for adopting her resolution which was substituted by House Resolution No. 1774, as well as the House leadership for taking cognizance of such an important initiative.
On motion of Rep. Banal, the Chair recognized
Rep. Isidro T. Ungab from the Third District of Davao City for his privilege speech.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.29,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F073
rows.title_full: THE NEED TO ADDRESS THE CHALLENGES IN VOLUNTEERISM BY THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ungab took the floor to give tribute to the
inspiring living heroes of the country and the Filipino people””the Filipino volunteers. He then described volunteerism as the purest form of service and bayanihan as an apt name for Filipino volunteerism. He expressed belief that the government has to unleash the unlimited potentials of volunteerism because it
needs the contribution and help of millions of Filipinos to overcome the development challenges being faced by the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 29,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F096
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE PASSAGE OF MEASURES SUPPORTING VOLUNTEERISM
rows.title_short: Tenth Year Anniversary Of The International Year Of Volunteerism
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Cinchona C.
Cruz-Gonzales from Party-List CIBAC thanked the
Filipino volunteers for their enthusiastic dedication and unyielding energy in serving and helping the nation soar to greater heights. She thereafter disclosed that the Committee on People´s Participation and certain Members of the House have already provided the necessary legal structure to foster volunteerism, citing
for instance the related resolutions of Reps. Cajayon and Ungab and the bills on volunteerism filed by Speaker Belmonte himself as well as by Rep. Loreto Leo “Leo” S. Ocampos. She then enjoined everybody to be part of citizen-based volunteer activities; and to continue to promote bayanihan and activities enhancing solidarity in the community and creating socially responsible citizens who will care beyond self and help others, and foster respect for other people.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 29,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G066
rows.title_full: VALUE OF VOLUNTEERISM TO NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND IDENTITY
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Edwin L.
Olivarez from the First Disctrict of Parañaque City, speaking in commemoration of the 10th anniversary of the International Year of Volunteers which was paralleled to the declaration of the United Nations (UN) Volunteers Programme, highlighted the contributions of the Philippines as a devout member of the UN Volunteers and as one of the largest suppliers of volunteers in the world.
He maintained that volunteerism in the country is
very much evident in the field of housing wherein
volunteers provide their personal time, energy and financial support to improve the need for shelter of the marginalized sectors. He then explained that society benefits greatly from volunteerism and that this exemplary Filipino trait should be further encouraged and inculcated in the people as a contribution to human development and as a tool of national development.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.29,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: C128
rows.title_full: CONTRIBUTION OF COOPERATIVES TO VOLUNTEERISM
rows.title_short: Significant Role Of Volunteers In Nation - Building
rows.abstract:
Rep. Paez claimed that the 10th Anniversary of
the International Year of Volunteerism provided him and the Committee on People´s Participation with a momentous opportunity to express their gratitude to the significant role of Filipino volunteers in nationbuilding and development and solidarity to the international volunteerism movement. He also delved into the history of voluntarism in the Philippines and extolled
the efforts of the following Filipinos and Filipino organizations who had contributed and shared their unique talents, efforts and resources to the society: Efren Peñaflorida Jr., for his help in the education of underprivileged children; the Gawad Kalinga Foundation Inc., for its pioneering efforts in providing low-cost housing projects to the poor; and the cooperatives´ sector, particularly those involved in providing for the basic necessities of the people, rescue and relief programs to victims of calamities, peace-building initiatives and environmental protection.
Rep. Paez also discussed the recent initiatives of the Committee on People´s Participation in institutionalizing and extolling volunteerism efforts in the country, particularly the adoption of pertinent House measures. In closing, he emphasized the importance of volunteerism as one of the most effective mechanisms for people´s participation and for achieving the common good.
(Source: House Journal No.29,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules

rows.author: G105
rows.title_full: \"WOMEN'S RIGHT, HUMAN RIGHT\"
rows.abstract:
Rep. De Jesus´ speech which she delivered in
Filipino focused on the forthcoming celebration of the International Human Rights Day and dwelt on several occasions, namely: the November 25th celebration of International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women; the November 29th Women Human Rights Defender´s Day and the anniversary of the First International Consultation of Women Human Rights Defenders; and the December 4th Manila Declaration of the 4th Regional Human Rights Defenders Forum. She claimed that these occasions underscore the importance of upholding and defending human rights in the country and the important
contributions of women human rights defenders and
their role in the elimination of human rights abuses. Thereafter, Rep. De Jesus enumerated the names of women human rights defenders who had become victims of human rights abuses and mentioned cases of extrajudicial killings during the past and the present administrations. In recognizing the role of women human rights defenders, she said that she had filed House Bills No. 5379 and 5580 which aimed to punish those who will violate the 1998 United Nations
Declaration of Human Rights Defenders and to
celebrate November 29 of every year as Women
Human Rights Defender´s Day, respectively.
(SOURCE: Journal No.29,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2012-02-06
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G108
rows.title_full: REDUCING CORRUPTION FROM AN ANGLE OF ADDRESSING THE NEEDS OF GOVERNMENT WORKERS
rows.title_short: Reforming And Strengthening Government Policies That Address Corruption
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Banal, the Chair recognized
Rep. Sherwin N. Tugna from Party-List CIBAC who
initially pointed out that the nation did not lack laws, jurisprudence, and institutions to address graft and corruption. He then opined that improving the basic needs of government employees and strengthening institutions that provide social security, would reduce the latter. He explained that if inadequate salaries
were raised and the delivery of medical, educational, insurance, housing and retirement benefits by state insurance agencies were enhanced, government workers would be less tempted to engage in anomalous activity. He stressed the need for a comprehensive and integrated national plan and relayed his
Party-List´s commitment in this regard.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.29,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2012-02-06
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G012
rows.title_short: Positive Action Against Continuing Degradation Of Mountains And Forests
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bataoil´s speech emphasized the need for
governmental and nongovernmental intervention to
address the continuing degradation of the country´s natural resources due to natural and man-made causes; the insufficient measures to address climate change; and the need for more improved sustainable development strategies. He cited, in particular, the need for immediate action on the adverse environmental degradation of the mountain ranges of his district due to typhoons, kaingin and illegal logging. Rep. Bataoil informed the Body that in the presence
in the Session Hall that day of barangay officials from the various municipalities of his congressional district, they were pledging their support and cooperation in the programs of the Administration to save the last remaining forests, mountains and rivers in their province.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.29,p.15)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-12-06)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS PERPETRATED AGAINST FARMERS
rows.title_short: Human Rights Violations Under The Aquino Administration.
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino in commemoration of the
Universal Declaration of Human Rights Day, Rep.
Mariano´s speech delved on the injustice and human rights violations being suffered by the Filipino farmers under the previous and present administrations. He said that to date, nothing is being done with regard to cases of extrajudicial killings, harassment and illegal arrests particularly in remote areas of the
country. He disclosed that the Committee on Human
Rights has yet to act on the resolutions he had filed calling for congressional inquiries into several cases of human rights abuses involving the Filipino peasants. He added that the family of President Benigno S. Aquino III, who owns Hacienda Luisita in Tarlac Province, had been blocking the distribution thereof to farmer-beneficiaries instead of giving justice to
those who had been killed for fighting for land reform. Thereupon, Rep. Mariano said that civil society and human rights advocates would soon hold a rally for freedom from impunity, justice, and a lasting peace that could only be attained by attacking the root causes of society´s problems.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.29,p.20)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G085
rows.title_full: HUMAN TRAFFICKING
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Sarmiento rose to underscore human trafficking as the gravest human rights challenge of the present time and almost a
universal problem and globally recognized as a
modern day form of slavery. He cited a specific case of human trafficking... and urged his
colleagues to support the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act which would strengthen the existing R.A.No. 9208 by stripping off human traffickers of the privilege of confidentiality, providing stiffer penalties to public officials conniving with traffickers, and stipulating the tasks of government offices in preventing victimization and rescuing and rehabilitating victims.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G090
rows.title_short: Impeachment Of Supreme Court Chief Justice Renato Corona; Resignation From The Majority And Chairman, Committee On Metro Manila Development
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tiangco rose to defend the integrity and independence of the House of Representatives on what he perceived as the railroading of the impeachment complaint filed against Supreme Court Chief Justice Renato C. Corona... However, he disclosed that they were not given a chance to read the Articles of Impeachment or to verify the facts and merits of the case since there was no debate and questions that ensued during the December 12 caucus. He pointed out for the record that he was not defending
the Chief Justice nor protecting former
President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo but only protecting the integrity and independence of the Supreme Court and other co-equal branches of government... Though he was grateful to Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr. for assigning him the chairmanship of the Committtee on Metro Manila Development, Rep.Tiangco stressed that the matter before him already transcends friendship ties...
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-12-12)

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: REACTION TO A NEWSPAPER ARTICLE RE: IMPEACHMENT AGAINST CJ RENATO CORONA
rows.title_short: Article  :  Signing Of Members Of The Impeachment Of C J Corona
rows.abstract:
Rep. Casiño took the floor to clarify the news article published in the day´s issue of the Philippine Daily Inquirer, which quoted his words that the Congressmen were clueless on the contents of the impeachment complaint against Supreme Court Chief Justice Renato Corona and that they were prevented from reading the complaint prior to its signing. He explained that said quote was accurate but it was made before the Majority caucus held on December
12, 2011, when the impeachment complaint was presented to the Members. He disclosed that the Makabayan Party-List Bloc, after holding a separate meeting and discussion subsequent to the caucus, decided to sign the complaint.
He maintained that the people had suffered for
nine years under the Arroyo Administration which he claimed had used the Legislature, the Judiciary, the military and the Commission on Elections to rob and cheat the nation. He said that Congress filed the impeachment complaint in question because the former President had been using Justice Corona to fight the accusations against her. He resented the insinuations that the Members were forced to sign the complaint
for fear of nonrelease of their pork barrel allocations, and suggested that those who signed the complaint under duress should withdraw their signatures. He expressed support to the impeachment complaint against Chief Justice Corona, and stressed that the Judiciary, as an independent body, should be the last bastion of justice.
(House Journal No.31,p.8-9
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G095
rows.title_full: CLARIFICATIONS ON SOME ISSUES RAISED BY REP. TIANGCO IN HIS PRIVILEGE SPEECH RE: IMPEACHMENT OF CJ RENATO CORONA
rows.title_short: Clarification On The Claims Of Tiangco That The Impeachment Of C J Corona Was Done In Haste.
rows.abstract:
Rep. Umali clarified certain issues raised by Rep. Tobias “Toby” M. Tiangco in his speech regarding the impeachment of Chief Justice Corona, to wit: 1) the impeachment process was not done with undue haste but in accordance with Section 4, Article XI of the 1987 Constitution and Section 13, Rule V of the House Rules on Impeachment Proceedings; 2) Committee on Justice Chairperson Niel C. Tupas Jr. thoroughly
explained the contents of the impeachment
complaint during the December 12 caucus and
Speaker Belmonte gave the Members the free will or the option to sign or not to sign the said complaint; and 3) the House of Representatives demonstrated its capacity to uphold the interest of the Filipino people without relinquishing its integrity and independence to a coequal branch by impeaching the Chief Justice. He reiterated that the House merely exercised its duty in impeaching Chief Justice Corona to effect
meaningful changes and to reform the Judiciary in
the name of good governance and in pursuit of the
President´s call for a straight path.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.31,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Golez R. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A007
rows.title_short: Reaction On The Privilege Speech Of Tiangco On The Impeachment Of C J Corona.
rows.abstract:
Rep. Apostol´s speech dwelt on how Rep.
Tiangco assaulted in his speech the previous day, the House leadership as well as the 188 Members who signed the impeachment complaint against Chief Justice Corona. He expressed the belief that the filing of complaint and initiation of the impeachment process against the Chief Justice was part of the due process
to which the latter was entitled, adding that the impeachment trial at the Senate was the proper venue for the latter to defend himself against all accusations being hurled at him.
Rep. Apostol then stressed that one should neither silence nor weaken the force of the voice of the majority as represented by the Members who signed the complaint, who are seeking truth and justice in behalf of the people.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.31,p.10)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-12-14)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F040
rows.title_full: ON THE POSSIBLE MOTIVES BEHIND THE AMBUSH OF REP. CANONIGO
rows.abstract:
Rep. Labadlabad condemned the recent attempt
on the life of Rep. Ranulfo P. Canonigo which he
said was an affront on the dignity of the House as an institution. Considering the desire of Rep. Canonigo to independently and genuinely pursue his Kakusa Party-List group´s advocacies, unrestrained by the influence of powerful people and vested interests, Rep. Labadlabad admitted to having been informed by certain reliable sources that the former had publicly made known in certain towns in Zamboanga Sibugay and Zamboanga del Norte about his frustrations and disappointments on the real intentions of
certain senior officials of his party-list organization and about the fact that he was pressured to resign as president of his own party-list group. Rep. Labadlabad said that the use of violence to attain one´s objectives is anathema in a representative democracy and that the culture of impunity should not be allowed to flourish any longer. In light of the present Administration´s crusade for good governance,
he urged the police not to leave any stone unturned in bringing the culprits to the bar of justice.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.31,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: REACTION TO ACCUSATIONS MADE AGAINST THOSE WHO SIGNED THE IMPEACHMENT COMPLAINT AGAINST CJ RENATO CORONA
rows.title_short: Alleged Railroading Of The Impeachment Of C J Corona
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello shared the sentiments just expressed
by many of his colleagues on the accusations leveled against Speaker Belmonte about the alleged railroading of the impeachment complaint against Chief Justice Corona; agreed with Rep. Golez (R.) that Chief Justice Corona delivered a highly politicized speech that afternoon which was unbecoming of his stature as the country´s highest magistrate; criticized the latter for accepting his midnight appointment by former
President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo and for being a
lapdog of the former president; and held the view
that the 188 Members who signed the complaint did
what was right for the people, which was to oust the Chief Justice who had bastardized the Supreme
Court, and that the Senate would uphold the said impeachment complaint.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.31,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E041
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED HER SENTIMENTS ON THE IMPEACHMENT OF CJ RENATO CORONA
rows.title_short: Trial Of The Three Branches Of Government
rows.abstract:
Rep. Magsaysay focused on the day´s burning issues which included the following, among others: 1)the events that had unfolded the past few days which culminated in the Body´s recent endorsement to the Senate of the Articles of Impeachment against Chief Justice Corona; 2) the widespread allegation that the 188 Members who signed the complaint did so without fully reading and understanding the complaint, given the volume of the documents involved and the
limited time of one hour, as manifested by the House Secretary General, within which said Members read and signed the complaint; 3) the right of the people,including the President, the Members of Congress, and the Chief Justice, to the freedom of speech; and 4) the present politicking among the three coequal branches of the Philippine government which could be detrimental to the needed government action on
priority matters, such as increasing oil prices and high unemployment rate. She challenged the Aquino Administration to release the PDAF allocations of five Members from the Minority, including hers, if the President was indeed
sincere in his pronouncements that he does not engage in politicking and political vendetta. She concluded that the real issue was not about President Benigno S. Aquino III or former President Arroyo, but about the government´s actions on the daily needs of their constituents.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.31,pp.10-11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: C045
rows.title_full: HIS PERCEPTION ON THE MAJORITY CAUCUS HELD ON DEC. 12, 2011 REGARDING THE IMPEACHMENT COMPLAINT AGAINST CJ RENATO CORONA
rows.title_short: Reaction On The Speeches Delivered By Some Members On The Impeachment Of C J Corona
rows.abstract:
Rep. Fariñas took the floor as an expert witness
to the impeachment proceedings against Chief Justice Corona, recalling that he was the first Representative of the 15th Congress to speak about the impeachment of Supreme Court members, not too long after the Body convened in July of 2010. He stressed that the impeachment complaint against the Chief Justice was a good one because all the members of the Majority arrived at a consensus when they were invited during the caucus and witnessed a Powerpoint presentation
on the eight Articles of Impeachment against Chief Justice Corona. He maintained that the House was merely upholding and being obedient to the Constitution when it acted as a referee between the President and the Supreme Court. He admitted to not having signed the complaint and refuted all insinuations that the House leadership pressured the signatories to the impeachmentresolution. He thereafter called on his colleagues to salute the House as an institution for doing its job, and not to cast doubts or motives on any other Member because this forms an unparliamentary conduct.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.31,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2012-01-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G014
rows.title_full: FLOODING IN CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY AND NEARBY AREAS
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. BENALDO
As he rose to fulfill a moral duty to his
constituents, Rep. Benaldo spoke on the December
16, 2011 tragedy that befell Cagayan de Oro City dueto Typhoon Sendong which saw endless accounts of
death and devastation. He then stated for the record
the magnitude of the catastrophe brought by the
typhoon upon the people of Cagayan de Oro City.
He thereafter expressed their heartfelt gratitude
to the persons, leaders and institutions who had lent a
helping hand and provided comfort to the victims of
the flash floods, specifically the following: the
country´s leaders, headed by the President and the
Vice President, for their immediate response and
commitment to rehabilitate Cagayan de Oro City;
Speaker Belmonte, for initiating the contribution of
P1 million assistance from every Member´s Priority
Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) allocation;
several Cabinet secretaries and officials, local
government officials, and his colleagues from both
the House and the Senate for their moral and
personal support; and nongovernment organizations
such as the UNICEF, the Philippine National Red
Cross and the World Vision. He then expressed hope
that given such tremendous support, his city would
be able to rise from the tragedy to become a stronger
and more prosperous place to live in.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F057
rows.title_full: FLOODING IN CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY, EXPRESSED GRATITUDE TO THE INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANIZATIONS WHO EXTENDED ASSISTANCE TO VICTIMS OF TYPHOON \"SENDONG\"
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF
REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
Rep. Rodriguez spoke on the details of the
devastation brought about by Typhoon Sendong in
Cagayan de Oro City, and how he, together with the
Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) in Camp
Evangelista, helped in the operations to rescue the
flood victims and how he thereafter joined the
Department of Social Welfare and Development
(DSWD) in the distribution of food and other relief
goods to the evacuation centers in his district.
On behalf of Rep. Benaldo, Cagayan de Oro City
Mayor Vicente Emano, and Reps. Yevgeny Vincente
B. Emano and Peter “Sr. Pedro” M. Unabia ofMisamis Oriental, he then expressed his deepest
gratitude to President Aquino, Vice President Binay,
Speaker Belmonte, the Members of the House and
the Senate and the heads of the different branches of
government, the Philippine National Police (PNP),
the AFP, and several local and international
nongovernment agencies for their help and cash
donations. He thereafter asked the support of the
Speaker and the Members of the House for the
approval of several measures which he and Rep.
Maximo B. Rodriguez Jr. had filed for the benefit of
their fellow Cagayanos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Biazon and Escudero; Manifestation by Rep. Ejercito. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G105
rows.title_full: IMPORTANCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTEDCTION AS A MEANS TO PREVENT CALAMITIES IN MINDANAO AND OTHER AREAS
rows.title_short: Long-range Solution Plan To Prevent Environmental Destruction.  Referred To The Appropriate Committee.
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. DE JESUS
In light of the discussions on the calamities that
happened in certain parts of Mindanao, Rep. De
Jesus, speaking in Filipino, warned that similar
tragedies could possibly happen throughout the
country because of the continued devastation of the
environment and the continued neglect of the
government on the matter by entering into mineral
production sharing agreements (MPSAs) and giving
consent to logging operations in Mindanao. She
belied reports that the mining sector contribute to the
economy and clarified that on the contrary, it posed
danger and destruction on the lives of the people. She
emphasized that the government should find
solutions on the matter and recognize the right of the
people to a safe and clean environment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F027
rows.title_full: NEED TO INVESTIGATE THE CAUSES OF SEVERE FLOODING IN CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY
rows.title_short: Inquiry On The Result Of The Flood In Cagayan De Oro
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. EMANO
Rep. Emano talked about the devastation that
struck the cities of Cagayan de Oro and Iligan which
he said could be attributed to the worsening climate
change and the reckless manner with which the
environment is being treated. Unlike the effort of
their political opponents of putting the blame on his
father, Cagayan de Oro City Mayor Vicente Y.
Emano, he stated that he was not interested in
trivializing and politicizing the tragedy but rather in
determining its real cause as well as finding ways to
mitigate its effects.
As such and in honor of those who had suffered
from the wrath of Typhoon Sendong, he said that he
would be filing a resolution calling for an inquiry into the cause of the severe flooding and deaths at the
height of the typhoon.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F118
rows.title_short: Allegation The He Maligned The Integrity Of The House
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. ALCOVER
Rep. Alcover took the floor to straighten
allegations that he had maligned the integrity and
credibility of the House as he referred to the events
that transpired after the Members´ signing of the
impeachment complaint against Chief Justice Corona
- that he would be made to answer any serious
offense he allegedly committed against the House
before the Ethics Committee and that the result
thereof could possibly lead to his expulsion from the
Chamber.
He emphasized that he never accused the
President of bribing the 188 Congressmen to sign
said impeachment complaint which he also stressed
when interviewed by Radio Station DYDD in Cebu
City and which got published as a news story in
Sunstar-Cebu and played up by the media in Metro
Manila.
He lamented the double standards being
practiced by certain House Members in dealing with
the so-called ethical issues, as he cited the case of
Rep. Ruben B. Ecleo Jr. who has remained scot-free
despite the issuance of a warrant of arrest against
him by the Sandiganbayan and the Cebu City
Regional Trial Court on charges of graft and
corruption and parricide, respectively; and Congress´
protective mantle of the infamous “Batasan Five.” He
cited rumors that the country´s leadership is moving
towards revolutionary governance to control all
branches of government, and called on the Majority
Leader and his other colleagues who were eager to
have him investigated to make good of what they
have been saying to the Filipino people; otherwise
they would be a disservice to the nation.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-01-16)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: ASSASSINATION OF GENERAL SANTOS CITY JOURNALIST KRIS GUARIN
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. BELLO
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Gunigundo, Rep. Walden F. Bello of Party-List
Akbayan spoke about the assassination of journalist
Chris Guarin of General Santos City, and expressed
fear that as the first media victim in 2012, he might
end up as another unsolved murder case. He pointed
out that to resolve senseless assassinations such as
this case, a mass-campaign approach must be
adopted which would involve the active participation
of civil society leaders and local and national
government representatives as well as strong pressure
from Congress.
Rep. Bello said that although he felt sad for the
family of Chris, he was also hopeful that his murder
has mobilized the civil society in GenSan, especially
the media, to work seriously with local government
officials with the help of the Aquino Administration,
thus the prospects for winning back the community
from the agents of impunity would not be negligible.
He concluded that a successful, coordinated mass
campaign against impunity could be a model for the
rest of the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F097
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR INVESTIGATION ON LOGGING AND MINING ACTIVITIES IN ILIGAN CITY, LANAO DEL SUR AND LANAO DEL NORTE
rows.title_short: Devastation Brought About By Typhoon Sendong In Cagayan De Oro And Iligan.
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE
OF REP. BELMONTE (V.)
Rep. Belmonte expressed his grief over the worst
calamity that ever occurred in his district which he
said was not caused by Typhoon Sendong but by a
few greedy people who had brought relentless destruction
to the environment through their illegal
logging and mining activities.
In behalf of the people of Iligan City, led by their
mayor and vice mayor, Rep. Belmonte expressed his
gratitude to Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr., Deputy
Speakers Raul A. Daza and Climaco, and all the
Members who have agreed to give a portion of their
salaries and Priority Development Assistance Fund
(PDAF) allocations to the Sendong victims in the
cities of Iligan and Cagayan de Oro. He also thanked
the President, the Vice President and the Cabinet secretaries
for all their support.
Rep. Belmonte also strongly recommended that
1) the House conduct an immediate investigation on
the pervasive logging activities in Iligan City, Lanao
del Sur and Lanao del Norte and immediately proseQUESTION OF PRIVILEGE
OF REP. BELMONTE (V.)
Rep. Belmonte expressed his grief over the worst
calamity that ever occurred in his district which he
said was not caused by Typhoon Sendong but by a
few greedy people who had brought relentless destruction
to the environment through their illegal
logging and mining activities.
In behalf of the people of Iligan City, led by their
mayor and vice mayor, Rep. Belmonte expressed his
gratitude to Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr., Deputy
Speakers Raul A. Daza and Climaco, and all the
Members who have agreed to give a portion of their
salaries and Priority Development Assistance Fund
(PDAF) allocations to the Sendong victims in the
cities of Iligan and Cagayan de Oro. He also thanked
the President, the Vice President and the Cabinet secretaries
for all their support.
Rep. Belmonte also strongly recommended that
1) the House conduct an immediate investigation on
the pervasive logging activities in Iligan City, Lanao
del Sur and Lanao del Norte and immediately prosecute
those responsible including their cohorts in the
government; 2) the national government, through the
Department of Environment and Natural Resources
(DENR), put a moratorium on all mining applications
and explorations in Iligan City; and 3) the national
government immediately appropriate funds to fast
track the rehabilitation and reconstruction of all public
infrastructures as well as the construction of
houses for the resettlement of the people whose
homes were damaged by the tragedy.
Rep. Belmonte then expressed his willingness to
coauthor the two resolutions already filed by Rep.
Rufus B. Rodriguez, which called for an investigation
on the supposed rampant illegal logging activites
in Iligan City and the two Lanao provinces and called
for an allocation of P2 billion for Cagayan de Oro
and Iligan.
Thereafter, the Chair recognized Rep. Marc
Douglas C. Cagas IV for his interpellation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Cagas, Fua and Palmones. Manifestation by Rep. Pangandaman (N). Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F048
rows.title_full: DELAYS IN IMPLEMENTATION OF INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS IN NORTHERN SAMAR
rows.title_short: Non-supply Of Construction Aggregates For Infrastructure Projects Due To Political Differences.
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE OF REP. ONG
Rep. Ong focused on the difficulties that he had
encountered in the implementation of infrastructure
projects in his province because of the refusal of
gravel and sand suppliers to deliver their products to
the contractors of the Department of Public Works
and Highways (DPWH), and which problem he
shares with some of his colleagues simply because
they do not belong to the same political party as the
provincial governor.
He disclosed the Provincial Board of Northern
Samar´s passing of an ordinance which in effect
amended the Government Procurement Reform Act,
and which, he surmised was an obvious exercise of
direct control in his province of all public biddings of
the national government. The same Board, he added,
also passed a resolution requiring government agencies
like the DPWH to withhold 10% of the gross
value on gravel, sand and other quarry materials,
which resulted in double taxation and the contractors´
stopping of their projects.
After manifesting his intent to include the letters
of the different contractors to the DPWH regional
director as forming part of his speech, Rep. Ong suggested
that the House craft a measure to stop the illegal
practice, and through a resolution, request the
President to disallow governors from imposing such
prohibition. He also asked the appropriate House
Committees to investigate his concern.
The Chair thereafter recognized Rep. Fua for his
interpellation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Fua and Garcia (P) Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: ALLEGED ILLEGAL LEASE AGREEMENT BETWEEN GLOBE TELECOM AND ALTIMAX BROADCASTING , INC.
rows.title_short: Franchise Grant To Altimax Broadcasting Company
rows.abstract:
Rep. Casiño spoke about the blatant violations
being committed by Altimax Broadcasting Co. Inc.
and Globe Telecom through its subsidiary Innove
Communications, with the possible knowledge of the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC).
He alleged, among others, that 1) the NTC
reversed its previous decision, denying Altimax an extension of the period within which it should
construct its radio and television stations after the Commission discovered that the company was nonexistent or not operational, because of the entry of Globe Telecom-Innove as Altimax´ new and controlling partner upon Globe´s payment of P160 million for the lease of the latter´s radio frequencies; 2) Altimax´ franchise is for operating radio and television stations and not for leasing radio frequencies to a telephone company; and 3) Globe Telecom has been cheating the government of millions of pesos in spectrum users fees because it is paying Altimax a much lower amount than what it would have paid the government. Rep. Casiño then urged Congress to investigate the matter immediately.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.33,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LEGISLATIVE FRANCHISES since 2012-01-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_short: His Resignation As Minority Leader; Term - Sharing For The Minority Leadership
rows.abstract:
Subsequently recognized by the Chair, Minority
Leader Edcel C. Lagman read into the records a text message which he said he received from a reliable source on January 4, 2012. He alleged that it confirmed a report that former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo had met with a few select
Oppositon members closely allied with her in order to replace him with Rep. Danilo E. Suarez as Minority Leader. He branded the message as
presumptuous propaganda for the Opposition´s
majority support for Rep. Suarez whereas the facts showed otherwise. Rep. Lagman maintained that the term-sharing agreement for the Minority leadership was baseless and nonexistent as said agreement was only limited to the speakership of the House when he and Rep. Suarez had agreed then to a term-sharing scheme if he would win said post in the House. Stating that the repeated incantation about a term-sharing agreement had become a repulsive refrain and in order to end further skirmishes within the Minority, he stated that he had irrevocably resigned as Minority Leader as he cannot continue to serve and lead a political group
that ignores independent, committed, competent and responsible leadership, among others. He said that he would now become an independent Member of the House as he cannot forsake his convictions for partisan concessions considering that he has serious policy differences with the Aquino administration. He then expressed his gratitude to the House Leadership, members of
the Opposition and congressional media and stated
that he would continue to fiscalize the Aquino
administration and pursue his agenda especially the Reproductive Health Bill. In conclusion, Rep. Lagman pointed out that although he and former President and now Rep. Macapagal-Arroyo both belonged to the Opposition, he was never a minion of the latter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.34,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-01-24)
rows.remarks: Manifestations by Reps. Villarosa and Suarez.

rows.author: F103
rows.title_full: CLIMATE CHANGE AND FOOD SECURITY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Guanlao focused on the ill effects of climate change which he attributed to man´s indiscriminate activities on earth, and how together with increasing human population, it has destroyed the earth´s environment and natural resources. He spoke in particular about land use conversion in the country, and for which reason he had filed House Resolution No. 1501, seeking a moratorium on land conversion application for the periods 2011 to 2016. He noted that national and local laws governing land use change and conversion are inconsistent and confusing, and that the government initiates action only when a disaster is forthcoming. He then urged the House to create a Special Committee on Climate Change and Mitigation; the
issuance by the President of an executive order
enforcing a moratorium on land use conversion; the review of the Local Government Code; and the
increase of the Department of Agriculture´s Quick
Response Fund for use by the small farmers and
fisherfolks during calamities and natural disasters.
(SOURCE:House Journal No.34,pp.5-6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOOD SECURITY since 2012-01-31
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Palmones; Manifestation by Rep.Escudero. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F104
rows.title_full: IN COMMEMORATION OF THE 1ST DEATH ANNIVERSARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCATE DR. GERRY ORTEGA
rows.abstract:
Rep. Palatino talked about the January 24, 2011
murder of radio talk show host and environment
advocate Dr. Gerry Ortega or Doc Gerry, the status of the police investigation of the killing and the case filed by the Department of Justice against the implicated Palawan politicians, and the alarming rise of human rights abuses suffered by environment advocates in the country. He surmised that if President Aquino and the House of Representatives were able to hasten the impeachment process of Supreme Court Chief Justice Renato Corona, the same should be done to address equally urgent issues such as the extrajudicial killings and the deep-rooted impunity in all branches of the government. In commemoration of Doc Gerry´s first death anniversary, Rep. Palatino again
urged Congress to revitalize efforts in swiftly
exercising its political power for Doc Gerry and all victims of extrajudicial killings, for environmental protection, and for ending impunity in the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2012-01-31
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: NEED FOR CONSULTATIONS REGARDING THE PROPOSED INCREASE IN PHILHEALTH PREMIUMS
rows.title_short: Recent Increase On The Premiums Of Phil Health
rows.abstract:
Committing to submit to the Body a written copy
of his complete speech, Rep. Bello said that overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) and migrant advocacy groups were questioning the 300% increase in Phil-Health premium contributions of OFWs and the lack of consultation with them regarding the matter. He said they were also concerned that the PhilHealth system deprived benefits for the dependents of single OFWs otherwise covered by insurance programs in the countries they were working in.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35.p.30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2012-02-07
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G067
rows.title_full: THE PHILIPPINE COCONUT INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Palmones focused on the need to control
scale insects that have been attacking coconut trees especially in the Province of Batangas, which if left unsettled would adversely affect a major dollarearner industry. He disclosed that the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) had released money to combat the infestation in Region 4-A but the amount was insufficient to implement its action plan. He also expressed
concern on the dwindling number of entomologists
in the country, whose expertise is more needed now due to climate change. He urged the Committee on Agriculture and Food to investigate the problem and requested his colleagues representing coconut-producing districts to provide the pertinent data that would help the authorities check the level of infestation of scale insects in their respective areas.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35,p.33-34)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2012-02-07
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Suarez, Romualdo and Padilla.  Manifestation by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: ON HIS ORDEAL IN A CEBU PACIFIC FLIGHT FROM ILOILO TO MANILA LAST JANUARY 22, 2012
rows.title_short: Delayed Flights Of Cebu Pacific Planes
rows.abstract:
Rep. Casiño narrated the ordeal he and his fellow
Cebu Pacific passengers suffered on their flight back to Manila from Iloilo on January 22, 2012 due to their plane engine´s malfunction: the long hours of departure delay; distress and tension; insufficient explanation on what had happened and what would be done; and thirst, hunger, and exhaustion. He said that their ordeal ended five hours later with majority
taking a smaller plane back to Manila, some riding the original plane after being repaired, and the rest rebooking their flights and demanding overnight accommodation from the airline. Thereupon, Rep. Casiño asked the Committee on Transportation to investigate the incident. He stressed that terms and conditions of some plane tickets enable airlines to escape from the provisions of the Civil Code on the safe transport of passengers to their destinations and provision of services during
delays and breakdowns, such as hotel accommodations, guaranteed seats, and official advice and information. He warned against the effects thereof on the country´s tourism industry
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35,pp.36-37)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2012-02-07
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G025
rows.title_full: EXPERIENCE OF A WOMAN:  A TRUE STORY OF MARCELINA SALANGO, WHO DIED GIVING BIRTH
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cojuangco briefly narrated the story of a
constituent who died from pregnancy and childbirth complications which she said could have been totally avoided if mothers were given access to appropriate health services. In this regard, she highlighted the need for the House to act on the Reproductive Health (RH) Bill as she joined President Benigno S. Aquino III in challenging the House leadership and in asking
the Members to put once and for all the Reproductive Health (RH) Bill to a vote. She opined that after many hours of debate on the measure, the Members have already exhausted all arguments relevant to the Bill and that additional debates would only further divide the House and would constitute an abrogation of the Members´ duty to their constituents.In closing, Rep. Cojuangco moved that the Body immediately consider a motion for closure on the debate
on the RH Bill and thereafter, to put the Bill to a vote. (Journal No. 36,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2012-02-14
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_full: ON THE CURRENT REFORESTATION PROGRAM IN MINDANAO
rows.abstract:
Rep. Romualdo informed his colleagues about the status of the memorandum of agreement entered
into by the Department of Environment and Natural
Resources (DENR) and foreign-owned Shannalyne,
Inc. in 1997 to undertake an industrial tree plantation and wood processing project in the Caraga Region and the integrated forest management agreements (IFMAs) issued by the Department to five corporations, including Shannalyne and the governments of New Zealand and Finland, in Agusan del Sur between 1998 and 2000. He thereafter stressed the need to review said contracts and agreements before the government proceeds further with its dealings with the corporations, this as he emphasized that said reforestation projects were expected to provide substantial jobs and business
opportunities to the host communities. If the agreements entered into by the DENR are found to be lopsided against the interest of the government, Rep. Romualdo suggested that these be
cancelled or rescinded at no cost to the Philippine government. He also urged Congress to use its oversight powers and investigate the matter and to prioritize the passage of legislations for the protection of the country´s forestlands.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,pp.31-32)
rows.status: Adopted on 2013-02-06
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Fua, Pangandaman (N) and Garcia (P). Referred to the appropriate committee.
