rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: ON ADOPTIVE CHILDREN AND PARENTS IN CELEBRATION OF THE \"ADOPTION CONSCIOUSNESS WEEK\"
rows.title_short: D S W D ' S Legal Adoption Of Children
rows.abstract:
In observance of the Adoption Consciousness
Week, Rep. Bataoil appealed for congressional support to the nationwide information drive of Social Welfare Secretary Corazon Soliman, urging Filipino families to legally adopt children to provide stable homes for the growing number of orphaned, abandoned and neglected children in the country. Rep. Bataoil said that the celebration of the Adoption Consciousness Week from February 4 to 10 aims to enhance public awareness on adoption processes and procedures and on the growing number of orphaned, abandoned or neglected Filipino children in need of love and permanent families. He added that there are accredited foundations that can help and assist families interested in adopting a child. In closing, Rep. Bataoil shared the poem “Legacy
of an Adopted Child” which he dedicated to the
Lady Legislators who may be similarly situated.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.34)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2012-02-14
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: ENSURE SOVEREIGNTY - INVESTIGATE RECENT DEVELOPMENTS US-RP RELATIONS
rows.title_short: Investigation On The Installation Of U S Military Facility In The Philippines.
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello delved on the recent developments in
US-Philippine relations which had been reported in the newspapers and stressed the need for Congress to monitor the decisions that the Aquino Administration is making in this area and to make positive contributions to crucial decisions, especially in the face of growing disagreement with the People´s Republic of
China over territories in the West Philippine Sea. He added that news about US intervention into the China-Southeast Asia conflict prompted the rightwing Chinese Communist Party newspaper Global Times to demand punishment to the Philippines through economic sanctions. He suggested that the Philippines employ multilateral diplomacy rather than allow increased US presence in the region. In sum, Rep. Bello stressed that Philippine sovereignty
rather than US hegemony must be ensured
and protected. He thus asked Congress to investigate America´s plans in the West Philippine Sea; the RPUS partnership against terrorism especially in the South; the alleged housing of a US facility in a Philippine
military base and its use for the rendition of
so-called “terrorists” to Third World countries; and the reported rotation of American troops from Japan to the Philippines.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.34)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2012-02-14

rows.author: A060
rows.title_full: WOMEN'S RIGHT TO HEALTH SERVICES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ocampo focused on certain women from Manila City whose lives have been burdened not only by poverty but also by the task of taking care of
a big family. She noted the government´s lack of
adequate family planning assistance, and stressed the need to create programs to protect the well-being of women in their multiple tasks as mothers, wives, workers and community organizers. She enjoined her colleagues to take women´s health as a serious national concern and recognize their reproductive rights by supporting the passage of the Reproductive Health
Bill.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: VIOLENT DEMOLITIONS
rows.title_short: Demolition In Barangay Corazon De Jesus, San Juan
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Ortega
(F.), Rep. Mariano of Anakpawis Party-List
who spoke in Filipino, condemned the demolition of urban poor dwellings under the Aquino Administration, in particular, the destruction a year ago of houses in Barangay Corazon de Jesus in San Juan City. He pointed out the refusal of local government of San Juan to recognize the rights awarded to the residents of said barangay due to the construction of the so-called San Juan “White House” or the new and modern City Hall of San Juan under the administration
of its City Mayor, Guia G. Gomez. He thereafter expressed his apprehension that projects and demolitions under the public-private partnership projects of the Aquino Administration were being implemented without clear planning and relocation sites for the relocatees and cited the study conducted by the Presidential Commission on Urban the Poor (PCUP) on the condition of the relocatees in resettlement areas.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.42)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G105
rows.title_full: WOMEN AFFECTED BY DEMOLITIONS
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Emmi A. De Jesus
of Gabriela Party-List, spoke about the problems
of relocatees in Southville B and C in Rodriguez,
Rizal regarding: the sub-meter scheme on electricity implemented by the Baque Corporation; the lack of potable water; lack of teachers and classrooms, inadequate health services; lack of employment and livelihood opportunities; the housing amortization and the quality of housing infrastructure and the
anomaly on housing contract. She thereafter enumerated several courses of action to benefit the residents of the demolished urban poor
household communities: 1) moratorium in
demolition orders by the government unless there is a sure relocation site; 2) government´s action in providing basic necessities in relocation sites; 3) investigation by government agencies of alleged anomalies committed by private developers; 4) government support funds for livelihood and employment projects; and 5) concrete measures to raise the human dignity of the relocatees.
REFERRAL OF REP. DE JESUS´ SPEECH
On motion of Rep. Ortega (F.), there being no
objection, the Body approved to refer the speech of
Rep. De Jesus to the appropriate Committee.
Thereupon, on motion of Rep. Ortega (F.), the
Chair recognized Rep. Raymond V. Palatino
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F104
rows.title_full: INTERNET FREEDOM
rows.abstract:
Rep. Palatino sought a definite congressional
stand on the issue of protecting the rights of Filipino citizens to freedom to information, in particular uncensored internet access to educational, research and social-networking websites, and the issue of expressing solidarity with the international community against the infringement of governments to the rights
of citizens to free speech and access to information. He claimed that the laws initiated and proposed by the US government, particularly the Stop Online Piracy Act (SOPA) and Protect IP (PIPA) Bills had been a cause for alarm for millions of internet users worldwide, websites such as Google and Wikipedia, and small business portals, compelling the internet community to launch the strike or the so-called “Blackout” to protest restrictions to information by the US government in enforcing copyright laws. He
added that the proposed laws had also threatened
internet users through submitted information content that is tantamount to censorship and violation of freedom of speech by government.
In closing, Rep. Palatino asked that Congress
remain vigilant against enacting laws that will curtail the freedom of speech and the rights of Filipino citizens to information.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.42-43)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: HUMAN TRAFFICKING OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE OF REP. ILAGAN
...Gabriela Party-List Representative Luzviminda C. Ilagan spoke about the recent case of women trafficking in Baguio City and noted the failure of Republic Act No. 9208 or the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act to address its mandate. She attributed poverty to the vulnerability of women and children to sex trafficking, and stressed the urgent need to craft measures that will
address the problem, as well as introduce
amendments imposing stiffer penalties against
traffickers without fear of retaliation on the part of the victims. (SOURCE: Journal No. 37,p.3)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G084
rows.title_full: COMMENDING THE FIRST 3 BOARD PLACERS OF THE 2011 CIVIL ENGINEERING LICENSURE EXAMINATIONS WHO ALL CAME FROM CATANDUANES STATE COLLEGES
rows.title_short: 2011 Civil Engineering Licensure Exam Top 3 Ranks From His Constituency
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sarmiento talked about his young
constituents, the three topnotchers in the recently held licensure examination for Civil Engineers given by the Professional Regulation Commission, namely: Benjie T. Pantino, Benjames T. Go and Jerwin DL. Rendon, who made a uniquely rare record for provincial schools when they got the first, second and third place, respectively, in said licensure examination. He said that the three were graduates of Catanduanes State Colleges who all came from families whose parents tried to make ends meet. He said that they were all worthy of citation and commendation considering the struggles they had to overcome to finish their education.
Moreover, Rep. Sarmiento underscored that this
is not the first time that the Catanduanes State
Colleges produced topnotchers in the field of civil and geodetic engineering. He stressed that the school´s roster of board topnotchers is an apparent indication of the quality of education that the institution is upholding and delivering to its students. Finally, Rep. Sarmiento shared the proud feeling of being like a father to his constituents and being one with their struggles and triumphs. (SOURCE: Journal No.37, p. 11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G085
rows.title_full: ESSENTIALS ON DISASTER RISK REDUCTION
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sarmiento discussed the 10 essentials in
building a disaster-resilient country, which include such factors as a country´s institutional and administrative framework, financing and resources, effective preparedness plan and recovery and reconstruction. He disclosed that together with other parliamentarians, he had been working with the UN
International Strategy for Disaster Reduction
(UNISDR) since the start of his term and that they had discussed in Geneva various ways of
mainstreaming disaster preparedness into the
planning and development agenda of governments.
He said that after undergoing strenuous
workshop in the UNISDR headquarters, he and his
colleagues came up with the Incheon Resolution,
highlighting the responsibility and need for
lawmakers to exercise their oversight function in the full implementation of existing laws which can play a bigger role in reducing disaster risks. He added that the Incheon Resolution embodies the commitment of the 16 House Members to ensure that a disaster
preparedness program is included in the national
budget. In closing, Rep. Sarmiento informed the Body that in the next two months, they would soon publish a checklist on these 10 essentials in order to guide the local government units (LGUs) in producing disaster-resilient
communities. (SOURCE: Journal No. 37, p.12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Ejercito. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A010
rows.title_full: COMMENDING THE SENATE ON ITS DECISION TO RESPECT THE TRO OF THE SUPREME COURT ON THE OPENING OF THE DOLLAR BANK ACCOUNTS OF CJ CORONA
rows.title_short: Commending Senate On Its Action On The T R O Issued By The Supreme Court On The Disclosure Of Foreign Deposits Of C J Corona
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aumentado spoke on the Senate´s political
will and judicial statesmanship in avoiding a
constitutional crisis when the latter, acting as an impeachment court, obeyed the temporary restraining order (TRO) issued by the Supreme Court (SC) prohibiting to open the Philippine Savings Bank (PSB) dollar account of SC Chief Justice Renato C.Corona. As the Senate ruling is anchored on constitutional and legal grounds, he stated however that the former had made it clear that it is prepared to argue its case on the merits and defend the legal and public policy grounds thereon. As he expressed support that a judgment in an impeachment proceeding is not subject to judicial review, Rep. Aumentado appealed to the SC to be more cautious and judicious in the exercise of its judicial power of review over issues related to the Corona impeachment trial and must reciprocate the
statesmanship of the Senate in order to prevent a
constitutional crisis. (Journal No. 37,p.13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: OIL PRICE HIKE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan spoke on the recent price increases of regular and premium gasoline products by the
country´s five giant oil companies and how they have been unconscionably raking in huge profits year after year amidst the nation´s economic crisis and the people´s poverty. She thereafter recalled that on January 27, 2011, she and Rep. Emmi A. De Jesus filed House Resolution No. 880 calling for an investigation into the price monitoring and regulatory system being implemented by the Department of Energy (DOE) in light of numerous allegations of overpricing against oil companies and recommending measures to protect consumers against the ill effects
of oil price increases.She said that to date, nothing had been done despite the promise of President Benigno S. Aquino III, together with the DOE, to open the book of accounts of these companies. As the voice of the poor and the marginalized women battered by unabated increases in the prices of oil and basic commodities, she urged the Members to look into and discuss proposals towards the removal of the value added tax (VAT) on petroleum products and the repeal of the Oil Deregulation Law. (Journal No.37,p.13-14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2012-02-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F035
rows.title_full: INTERNATIONAL LANGUAGE DAY
rows.title_short: Use Of First Language Or Mother Tongue In Basic Education
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Gunigundo said that
the commemoration that day of the International
Mother Language Day with the theme “Mother Language Instruction and Inclusive Education” was very timely in view of the implementation by the Department of Education (DepEd) beginning June 2012 of the K-12 basic education program, using the mother tongue-based multilingual education (MTB-MLE) approach in public schools nationwide. He then aired his concern regarding the following issues, among others: 1) the preparedness, capability and willingness of the DepEd leadership to implement a broad and comprehensive basic education program using the MTB-MLE approach as promised by President Benigno S. Aquino III; and 2) the need
for DepEd to seriously consider the difficulties being encountered by young school children in understanding class lessons being taught in a language foreign to them. He thereafter cited the achievements thus far made by education reform advocates, including him and the teachers and officials of DepEd-Valenzuela Division, in pursuing the adoption of the MTB-MLE throughout the country. On the proposed K-12 curriculum, Rep. Gunigundo then posited a transition period from the primary to secondary language of from six to eight years instead of merely three. He also suggested that the curriculum underscore the goal of basic education of speaking, writing and thinking fluently in the first language; recognize that oral language development
is a prerequisite of both first and second language literacy; reinstate science as a separate subject beginning Grade 1; use cultural and local concepts in teaching science, math, and social studies; and teach students to think instead of merely memorize. To conclude, Rep. Gunigundo stressed that the government should not stop pursuing and investingin its education agenda because of the huge price that the country would pay for the illiteracy that would
result from its present educational system.
(Journal NO. 37,pp.25-26)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2012-02-28
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Padilla, Apostol, Lagman and Garcia, P.

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: PLIGHT OF EMPLOYEES IN THE CIVIL REGISTRAR'S OFFICE
rows.abstract:
Saying that February is Civil Registry Month,
Rep. Bataoil pointed out that civil registry personnel fulfill their vital role in securing proofs of identity and status of the country´s citizens despite various difficulties encountered. He asked his colleagues to help promote and improve their social and economic
well-being, define their functions and responsibilities vis-a-vis the National Statistics Office (NSO), develop the skills and capabilities of local government units to enable them to deliver mandated programs in civil registration, and improve the services of both national and local civil registries. (Journal No.38,p.1)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2012-02-28
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G092
rows.title_full: ALLEGED HARASSMENT COMMITTED BY SOME LOCAL OFFICIALS IN THE RECOUNT FOR THE TAGUIG MAYORALTY POSITION
rows.title_short: Decrying The Move Of The Cayetanos To Block The Retrieval Of Ballot Boxes In Taguig City Hall
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tinga decried the mayor and local government of Taguig City for preventing a
Commission on Elections (Comelec) team to carry
out a lawful order to retrieve ballot boxes in the city hall. He referred in particular to the election protest filed by former Supreme Court Justice and former Rep. Dante O. Tinga against Taguig City Mayor Lani Cayetano, and the failure by the Comelec to retrieve the ballot boxes because of the barricade in the City Hall being made by the latter´s supporters every time a retrieval order was served. He appealed to Malacañang to prevent the miscarriage of justice in the city by providing Comelec with security in counteracting said illegal acts as well as allowing the Department of Public Works and Highways to finish the national projects it
has started therein but which the local government had stopped. (Journal No.38,pp.1&2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2012-02-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G039
rows.title_full: PRESERVING THE SANCTITY OF THE PINAGLABANAN SHRINE
rows.title_short: Real Story Behind The Demolitions In San Juan City
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Ejercito elaborated on his disagreement to the subject of the February 13, 2012 speech of Rep. Rafael V. Mariano, regarding the alleged unwarranted demolition by the local government of San Juan of urban poor settlements in a land adjacent to what is known as the Pinaglabanan
Shrine. He maintained that the land that had been
occupied by the informal settlers is owned by the
State and the issue of the ownership of said property had already been resolved through the issuance of Proclamation No. 1716 by then Pres. Ferdinand Marcos who, exercising his legislative powersthrough Amendment No. 6, allocated certain portions of land of the Pinaglabanan Shrine to the local government of San Juan for building public infrastructures. He claimed that the basis for the alleged right of the informal settlers to occupy the aforementioned property, which was Proclamation No. 164, cannot supersede or amend the aforementioned law as stated in the decision of the court in the case of Municipality of San Juan, Metro Manila vs. Court of Appeals, DENR, and Corazon De Jesus Homeowners, Incorporated. After discussing the other reasons for the demolition of the urban poor settlement in San Juan, he underscored that its local government is not inured to the complaints and pleas of the informal settlers.
He then cited several programs when former
President Joseph “Erap” Estrada was the town mayor up to the time he became the city mayor and until the present administration of his mother, Mayor Guia Gomez, which would benefit the local government of San Juan and address the relocation and basic needs of the urban poor communities. In closing, he stressed that the leaders of San Juan would not be deterred in doing something if it would benefit the whole society. (Journal No.38,pp.17-18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cagas. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: C403
rows.title_full: FOOD SECURITY
rows.title_short: Foreign Land Grabbing In The Philippines
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Rodolfo G. Biazon from the Lone District of Muntinlupa City expressed concern about
the government´s policy to allow China to use
Philippine lands to produce food for the consumption of its citizens. He cited historical facts and various data and statistics and pointed out that the country´s population growth has grossly outpaced and will continue to overtake its food production especially as
regards rice. He also mentioned the several
memoranda of agreement and agri-business deals
between public and private agencies of the two
countries as he asked whether the Philippine
government could provide basic sustenance to its
own people and stressed that a good, empowered,
and contented citizenry was a key to development
and peace and order. He further cited the millions of still unirrigated lands in the country and inquired if current policies on land use for food production were still viable or antiquated as to require remedial legislation.
Recognizing that the country needs to have
agreements with other international communities to ensure its economic existence, Rep. Biazon
maintained however that said agreements should
adhere to and be in harmony with the Constitution
and other existing laws and that economic policies of the government must be characterized with sound firmness that is protective of the country´s naturalresources without sacrificing patrimony and selfrespect for food security. He then pointed out that a country that can ensure the sustainability of its food sources for the people will be a very secure nation in the future.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOOD SECURITY since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Albano and Aumentado. Referred to the Cttees. on Agriculture and Food; the Special Cttee. on Food and Security and Natural Resources.

rows.author: G105
rows.title_full: JUSTICE FOR VICTIMS OF SEXUAL VIOLENCE COMMITTED BY MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND POLICE
rows.title_short: Rape Cases Committed By Members Of The A F P
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino to commemorate the
worldwide celebration of the International Women´s Day on March 8, Rep. De Jesus delved on the appeal for justice of women victims of sexual abuse and violence, discussing in particular the cases of women who were raped by men in uniform. In this regard, she informed the Body of a Resolution she had filed urging the House to investigate such cases and to scrutinize and strengthen the implementation of the provisions of the Anti-Rape Law especially as far as the so-called protectors of the law are concerned. She then expressed hope that every celebration of the International Women´s Day would be a triumph for every woman in their fight against any endeavor, including any fight for their honor and reputation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.19
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G128
rows.title_full: LEGISLATIVE AGENDA FOR THE PROVINCE OF ZAMBALES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ebdane provided an update to the Filipino
people and to the Members of the House of
Representatives on the new and improved Province
of Zambales, citing in particular the achievements of the new provincial government in the areas of public infrastructure, sports, health and wellness, governance and public accountability. In fulfillment of his promise to his fellow Zambaleños, he cited his legislative priorities for the next 15 months to include the following, among others: to promote tourism in the province by declaring Mt. Pinatubo as an eco-tourism zone and Mt. Tapulao as a tourist spot and recognizing the importance of preserving and sharing the culture of Aetas; to focus on the needed infrastructures in the community to include water systems for the remaining barangays which still need modern facilities; to construct more public school buildings in rural and remote areas and barangay health buildings; to build a merit-based educational assistance program to raise the level of excellence of
the youth in Zambales to world-class standards and to match educational opportunities with job
requirements and availabilities to ensure higher
chances of employment for his constituents; and to pay more attention to the procurement standards for sports equipment and training programs for sports development. In closing, he said that he is honored to be part of
the House of Representatives and more honored to
represent the people of his district.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G063
rows.title_full: CURRENT STATE OF HUMAN TRAFFICKING IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
As he recalled in Filipino his concern about the
victims of human trafficking, Rep. Pacquiao shared the good news that the Philippines was no longer in the Tier 2 Watch List of the Trafficking in Persons Report 2011 published by the US Department of State. He revealed that since his last speech on the subject, the country had sent to jail more than twice the number of traffickers in the last seven years and
then commended the President for his leadership in addressing the problem. He also honored some Filipinos who were recognized by the US Department of State for their good work in preventing human trafficking. Rep. Pacquiao thereafter appealed for the immediate approval of the proposed amendments to the Anti -Trafficking in Persons Law or Republic Act
(R.A.) No. 9208 by increasing the penalties for violations thereof and for the immediate passage of the Magna Carta for Domestic Workers to lessen cases of trafficking of domestic workers abroad. He added that the combination of the passage of these two laws would keep traffickers and their cohorts on the ropes. Lastly, he recommended the strengthening of the government´s witness protection program; integrating trafficking and other migration concerns in the regular curricula; empowering local governments to guard their own areas against traffickers; and for the
Office of the Ombudsman to intensify its drive
against corruption in trafficking cases as well as for the courts to prioritize and fast-track the resolution of these cases.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,pp.25-26)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cagas. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G123
rows.title_full: WELFARE OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the Chair
recognized Rep. Catalina C. Bagasina from Party-
List ALE or the Association of Laborers and
Employees who spoke in Filipino to ask her
colleagues to support House Resolution No. 1023,
urging the Social Security System (SSS) and the
Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) to encourage
host countries of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) to sign bilateral social security agreements regarding equality of treatment, export of benefits, totalization of  contributions, creditable periods, payment of
benefits, and mutual administrative assistance. She said that the agreements would enable around nine million OFWs to annually transfer almost P500 billion in social security contributions from their host countries to the SSS, thereby generating millions of jobs and businesses; raising the standard of living of OFWs; and spurring economic development. She also explained the provisions of the agreements and pointed out that the ALE Party-List was continuing dialogues with government agencies
concerned to increase the number of countries which have signed the same.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.38)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Padilla. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: INDISCRIMINATE LARGE-SCALE MINING IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Teddy A. Casiño from Party-List Bayan Muna spoke on the dangers and destruction brought about by large-scale open-pit mining in the country, and expressed support to the call for a ban thereto. He disclosed that the Committee on Natural Resources recently approved two resolutions supporting the mining moratoriums enacted via local ordinances by the provincial governments of Negros Occidental and Capiz, and cited other local efforts to stop open-pit mining throughout the country. While he recognized mining as essential to nation-building, he lamented that this is being done
at the expense of the environment and the future
generations but to the benefit of foreign companies and industries. He cautioned that as the country celebrates the 17th year of the Mining Act of 1995 on March 3, an executive order is expected to be issued soon, which would favor rich and influential mining corporations all in the name of revenues needed for national development. Together with an appeal for the President not to sign said executive order, he urged his colleagues to repeal the Mining Act and to enact a new peoplecentered mining law which will, among others: 1) establish a centralized and strategic planning of the
mining industry through the implementation of a
national industrialization program and a national
mining plan; 2) conserve and develop the country´s minerals towards national industrialization but with due regard to the interests of the nation´s lands, biodiversity, indigenous people´s customary laws, and local governments; and 3) impose a clear set of
“no gold zones” for mining.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,pp.39-40)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-03-06
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Padilla, Pangandaman (N.),Sarmiento (M.S), Mandanas, Ong and San Luis. Referred to the approrpriate committee.

rows.author: G047
rows.title_full: ON THE HEALTHY LIFESTYLE PROGRAM CURRENTLY BEING IMPLEMENTED IN HIS DISTRICT
rows.title_short: Healthy Lifestyle Program In Bacolod City
rows.abstract:
Rep. Golez (A.) spoke about a dance exercise
routine called Jam Step, which he spearheaded in
elementary and high schools in his district in line with the advocacy of the Department of Health´s Healthy Lifestyle Program. He noted how
globalization and social changes have influenced the spread of noncommunicable or life style/degenerative diseases, especially among the poor andbdisadvantaged population, and stressed the need for a more challenging health policy and system to address this concern. He said that it was for this reason that he, together with the Ang Batang Pinoy Movement,
came up with a simple dance program that was fun
and easily accepted by the students, with the hope that it would be adopted by schools and implemented after their respective flag ceremonies through the use of a music video.
He then urged his colleagues in Congress to
support the Jam Step and lead in the advocacy for
children to start the discipline of having a healthy lifestyle and expressed hope that all the children in his colleagues´ districts would join the children of Bacolod City in July 2012 for Jam Step Philippines.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,pp.7-8)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2012-03-13
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F061
rows.title_short: Expressing His Gratitude To His Colleagues For Condoling With This Family On The Death Of His Father
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Ferdinand Martin
G. Romualdez stated that he would like to rise on a question of personal and collective privilege to express his gratitude to the House leadership led by Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr., Majority Leader Neptali M. Gonzales II, Minority Leader Danilo E. Suarez, the Members of the Minority and the Majority, his close friends Reps. Joseph Victor G. Ejercito, Emmeline Y. Aglipay, Rachel Marguerite B.bDel Mar, Antonio F. Lagdameo Jr. and Tobias “Toby” M. Tiangco who were principal authors of House Resolutions No. 2169, 2172, 2175, 2176 and 2177, expressing condolences to his family on the passing of his father, the late Benjamin Romualdez, former
ambassador and governor of the Province of Leyte.
Rep. Romualdez also stated that the expression
of support and solidarity during this very difficult time in their life had definitely helped him and his family to carry on and that he would like to thank everyone for taking time out to come visit them during his wake to offer their condolences. He further stated that had former Ambassador Romualdez taken his seat in the 1978 Interim Batasan Pambansa, he would have also been accorded the respect and privileges befitting a deceased former member of the Chamber, as in the case of the late Rep. Ignacio “Iggy” T. Arroyo Jr. In closing, he expressed his gratitude to all the Members of the House for condoling with his family.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-03-05)

rows.author: F071
rows.title_full: PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP IN CARP
rows.abstract:
Speaking about the role of landowners in
national industrialization, Rep. Teves suggested that landowners who were paid millions in bonds under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program
(CARP), be encouraged to invest in public-private
partnership projects (PPPs) such as railroads,
highways, airports, and export processing zones. He explained that this will not only attain the objective of social justice but also industrialization.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,p.25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2012-03-13
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: COCO LEVY FUND
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello initially remarked that former
Agrarian Reform Secretary Horacio “Boy” Morales,
who recently passed away, had aggressively pushed
for the recovery and distribution of the coco levy fund to coconut farmers as it was they who needed it most. He then stated that in early 2012, the Supreme Court (SC) had ruled that the coco levy funds, comprising 24% of shares in San Miguel Corporation (SMC), are owned by the government and should be used only for the benefit of all coconut farmers and for the development of the coconut industry. He
pointed out that the government must not squander
this opportunity and make decisive strides towards rural poverty alleviation and most importantly, to rectify historical wrongdoings by making sure that the money stays intact and does not leak to those who do not have the interests of the farmers in mind.
Thereupon, Rep. Bello made the following
recommendations: 1) to create a trust fund that will make sure that the money is not reposed in only one agency, such as the Coconut Industry Investment Fund (CIIF) or the Philippine Coconut
Administration (Philcoa); 2) to include coconut
farmers in the decision-making processes in the
utilization of the money; 3) to conduct a
comprehensive audit of all the government sequestered entities which were created with the
coco levy funds; and 4) for the government to pursue other coco levy-related cases and secure a favorable decision on the same.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,pp.25-26)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND FISHERIES since 2012-03-13
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Fua. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G061
rows.title_full: ECONOMIC, POLITICAL AND SOCIAL ACHIEVEMENTS OF WOMEN AROUND THE WORLD
rows.abstract: Rep. Mellana rose to mark the economic, political and social achievements of women around the world; discussed the state of women in the workforce where surveys show that the playing field is yet to be leveled and inequities are yet to be redressed as there are remaining policy gaps and complex socio-cultural realities that need to be addressed to achieve gender parity; stressed that women workers should be provided with ... support to their special needs; stressed that the Labor Code needs to be reviewed to be able to adapt and be responsive to the needs of women workers in the formal, informal and migrant sectors, among others, concluded that to advocate gender equality is not to advocate for women alone, but for the greater good of all.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G119
rows.title_full: WOMEN IN THE 21st CENTURY: LEADERS, BUILDERS AND SUSTAINERS OF PHILIPPINE DEVELOPMENT
rows.title_short: Role Of Women In National Development
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cortuna discussed the role of women in a rapidly changing world and their common and
collective resolve as a society, people and nation to overcome all obstacles and to rise in the community of nations; stressed that women had gradually emerged as partners, participants, leaders, builders, and enablers in the development of the country and in the advancement of good governance and accountability; stated that the government has
made successful strides in promoting women´s rights and welfare as well as in recognizing the
indispensable role of women in national development; noted that the issue of gender and development (GAD) policy was not being faithfully complied with which requires all government bureaus, departments and agencies to set aside a minimum of 5% of their appropriations for GAD-related activities; sought the cooperation and support of the DOF, DILG, and the COA to be more proactive in advancing gender mainstreaming policies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Apostol. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: BALIKATAN EXERCISES BETWEEN US AND PHILIPPINE ARMED FORCES
rows.title_short: Joint Phil - U S Military Exercises
rows.abstract: Rep. Ilagan questioned the real motive behind the so-called humanitarian missions being conducted by the U.S. Armed Forces...; expressed fear that through said military exercises, the US government also effectively maps and surveys Philippine natural resources...; added that the exercises also cause displacement of communities and highlight the vulnerability of women and girls to abuse; underscored the need ...to call to action Filipino women to rise in defense of the motherland to seek justice and peace. Proposed that the Chamber initiate measures to protect women and children, the country´s resources as well as patrimony and sovereignty from unjust US impositions. Recommended the termination of all inequitable treaties and military agreements of the Philippines with the US...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G046
rows.title_full: WOMEN EMPOWERMENT
rows.title_short: Significant Role Of Women In The Country
rows.abstract: Rep. Go ... emphasized that women had gone far ...to excelling in various fields of endeavor due to equal opportunities and exposure to education; ... claimed that Filipino women had equaled Filipino men in terms of achievements and even excelled in their chosen vocations to make important and immense contributions to Philippine society, education, culture and politics; enumerated several of these exemplary and distinguished Filipino women...; informed the Body that she is also the 1st woman legislator in her congressional district; proposed for a comprehensive review of the high school curriculum in the country to incorporate therein a subject that will specifically focus on the rights of women, their role in nationbuilding, and gender equality.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G034
rows.title_full: DISCRIMINATION AGAINST MUSLIM FILIPINO WOMEN
rows.abstract:
Rep. Quibranza-Dimaporo argued ...the need to recognize the rights of Muslim Filipino women in a multicultural society; maintained that Muslim Filipino women have to exercise these rights because of the discrimination they had experienced from the lack of understanding of
cultural diversity and inability to comprehend
religious and cultural practices of Muslim Filipinos. These issues of discrimination ... had also resulted to prejudicing their rights to observe practices of their Muslim religion while attending secular universities; asked that the Body consider reviving and supporting previous measures or introduce new ones aimed at promoting the rights of all, including Muslim Filipino women since this would be their way of honoring Muslim women who had excelled and carved their niche in various fields of endeavor and had contributed to the progress of society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G017
rows.title_full: EMPOWERING WOMEN
rows.abstract:
Rep. Calixto-Rubiano talked about the roots of women´s movement and the achievements of several Filipinas or Pinays, such as Wan Ling Martello, who is the incoming chief financial officer of food giant Nestle, the late President Cory Aquino, singers Lea Salonga and Charice Pempengco, White House executive chef Cristeta Pasia Comerford, international designer Josie Natori, breastfeeding specialist Nona-Andaya-Castillo, and boxer Ana “The Hurricane” Julaton. Also commended the women topnotchers in the recent bar examinations. Underscored that the
successes of these women have inspired many who
want to make something of themselves thus proving
to the world that a woman can lead and excel and can truly make a difference.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Query of Rep. Rodriguez (R.).  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G065
rows.title_full: UNBRIDLED FELONIES CONTINUOUSLY COMMITTED BY THE NOTORIOUS KURATONG BALELENG GROUP
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ocampos spoke on the continued threat to national security posed by the organized crime
syndicate Kuratong Baleleng and enumerated
their alleged involvement in armed robberies, kidnappings, guns for hire, armed bank robberies,
murder, and illegal drugs in Metro Manila and in
the provinces; Maintained that Kuratong Baleleng´s continued impunity in Ozamiz City and in nearby localities should be a cause for alarm for the government...Because of its threat to national security, he then proposed the dismantling of Kuratong Baleleng.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2012-05-08

rows.author: E032
rows.title_full: DETERIORATING HEALTH CARE SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Garin relayed her recent experience with a
medical clinic inside a Quezon City mall which
mixed up her x-ray results with another patient´s. She said that her first result showed tuberculosis and emphysema while the succeeding one stated normal chest findings. She pointed out that if she and her copatient accepted the initial results, she could have suffered from believing that she had infected her husband who had undergone surgery and the other patient could have not started treatment for his
illness. As she considers her experience a reflection of how the delivery of healthcare services in the country has been converted into a commercial commodity, Rep. Garin inquired 1) whether healthcare provision has evolved into a highly commercialized service; 2) who protects the patients especially those with minimal medical knowledge; 3) what a doctor´s signature means; 4) whether companies are meticulous in choosing healthcare providers; 5) the
availability of measures to correct the damage done especially for walk-in patients; and 6) whether the Department of Health (DOH) and the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) are looking into the situation. In view of the foregoing and as she denounced the commercialization of medical practice, Rep.
Garin moved that the Committee on Health,
specifically the Subcommittee on Oversight, should investigate the matter and act accordingly
(SOURCE: House Journal No.47,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2012-05-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.
